Executive summary

Faster, findable and compliant

The current site is a WordPress + Elementor build. It is slow on phones, its pages are thin and hard for Google and AI assistants to understand, and some wording conflicts with the Law Society of Ontario’s advertising rules. The new site fixes each of these. Every figure below was measured.

What holds the current site back

  • Visitors land on a “gateway” splash page and must click again to reach the real home page.
  • Practice pages average 105 words — too little to rank or be quoted by AI assistants.
  • No Google descriptions, no facts about the firm or lawyers for Google, no tracking, a broken robots.txt.
  • 10 leftover test and course pages are public, plus WordPress’s “Hello world!” post on the home page.
  • “You Deserve The Best Lawyer” and “We specialize in” conflict with LSO advertising rules.

What the new site delivers

  • Civil litigation leads, with ten in-depth practice pages (6,826 words vs 943).
  • Every lawyer and the paralegal shown with a verified Law Society number.
  • Elegant, fast animation that switches off for people who prefer reduced motion.
  • Call, WhatsApp and enquiry one tap away on every phone screen.
  • Every old address kept or redirected (54 rules), so existing rankings carry over.

6 · Trust & Law Society compliance

Accurate, verifiable, rule-aware

For a law firm, an inaccurate claim costs more than a lost ranking — and AI assistants repeat what a website says.

“You Deserve The Best Lawyer” and “We specialize in”
LSO rules limit “specialist” wording to certified specialists and require verifiable claims. Replaced; an automated check now blocks these words, even inside schema.
Pakistan-called associates listed beside Ontario lawyers
All kept, as requested, with a clear note that they support research and drafting under the firm’s Ontario lawyers.
Credentials not verifiable from the site
Checked on the LSO and CICC registers on October 3, 2026: Murad Ali Khan #67403V, Louis Townsend #66502E, Himani Attri #94301E, Devender Kumar #P20192, Ayad Al Basha #R705576.
“Himani Attari” on the team page
The LSO directory and her LinkedIn spell it “Attri” — the new site uses Attri; please confirm.
A watermarked Shutterstock silhouette as a team photo
Not reused (licensing risk); a monogram shows until a real portrait arrives.
12 different phone numbers; “City Center” and “City Centre”
One consistent name, address and phone everywhere, with WhatsApp and fax clearly labelled.
A public 2019 “friends & family” price list
No fees appear on the new site, per your instruction.

9 · Why Google decides who gets the call

Three places on Google, before any website

When someone searched “lawyer mississauga” on October 3, 2026, Google showed a map with three firms — and one paid slot — above every normal result. Maks was not among them.

  1. Google Ads — paid results at the very top for the searches you choose (“civil litigation lawyer mississauga”). Two firms were advertising on that search.
  2. The map pack — three firms from Google Maps. Google says it ranks them on relevance, distance and prominence, and that “more reviews and positive ratings can help your business’s local ranking.”
  3. Organic results — the website. This is what the new site is built for.

Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode draw on the same Business Profiles and reviews for local questions, so the profile now shapes AI answers too.

Google, “lawyer mississauga”, October 3, 2026, Mississauga location, signed out. Ranking factors: Google Business Profile Help, “Tips to improve your local ranking on Google”.

Where Maks stands today

  • The Business Profile appears unclaimed (“Own this business?”).
  • 43 reviews at 4.3 ★, against 93–2.1K for the map-pack firms.
  • Not on page 1 for either search we checked; not advertising.
  • Instagram and Facebook list a different office number from the website.

What we would do

  • Claim and complete the profile: categories, services, photos, weekly posts, Q&A.
  • A steady, genuine review routine with a direct link — never incentivised.
  • Google Ads on civil litigation and your other priority areas, with call and form tracking and Law Society-compliant ad copy.
  • Monthly Maps rank tracking so you can see the movement.
